selectionPolicy: Retain every brand/organization logo among the 92 existing independent exports. Separate flags, public symbols, icon/diagram calibrations and retired duplicate IDs. Add eight named independent evaluation exports selected by brand/structural diversity before source retrieval or candidate measurement.
representativenessLimits: Public-domain, self-contained, path/primitive exports available through Commons; brand and organizational identities including civic/club marks. This is a first 27-document cohort, not a random market sample. The 19 retained exports have historical measurements/tuning; only the eight newly predeclared exports are fresh holdouts.
holdoutPolicy: No document-specific tuning on the eight new evaluation holdouts. Select shared mechanisms from the retained development corpus; reevaluate every frozen case after shared changes. Preserve all outcomes and gaps.
variantPolicy: Small/intended/large x transparent/white/black, outputScale 1. Retain prior numeric viewport obligations as additional named cases. Integer logical viewport choices precede fresh candidate comparison. Only root dimensions and existing root-style width/height change in oracle materialization. Without a source viewBox, scaled sizes add an intrinsic-CSS-size viewBox and BOTH renderer and browser consume that explicitly hashed variant. Original files and historical references remain unchanged. ViewBox-bearing variants render the original SVG with explicit viewport options.
oraclePolicy: Recipe 3, win64 pinned Chrome. Three sequential fresh processes per new configuration, all healthy/cleaned and byte-identical. Preserve original Ford references. A new capture is never accepted because it matches the candidate. Transport failures, rejections, known differences and unmeasured cases retain their frozen denominator.

documents.name: Coca-Cola
documents.normalization: Only line endings normalized to LF under repository SVG policy; original upstream bytes separately hashed.

licenseMetadata.ImageDescription: Wordmark of Coca-Cola, trademarked by The Coca-Cola Company, but because the logo is simply "Coca-Cola", there is no proof as to who originally wrote it. Master Penman Louis Madarasz (1859-1910) was said to have told one of his students that the work was his own. When the work was created, Madarasz had a mail order business, could have illustrated the logo, and the writing style is similar to his. In the book "An Elegant Hand" by William E Henning, it states that Frank Mason Robinson, who was the bookkeeper of the firm, originated the name Coca-Cola and specified that it be written in Spencerian Script. In a 1914 court case, Robinson testified that he was "practically the originator" and that "some engraver here by the name of Frank Ridge was brought into it". Thus the logo itself has no currently copyrightable authorship and its exact creator is unknown. In any case, the trademarked Coca-Cola logo was published numerous times in the United States (its country of origin) before 1923, and so is now ineligible for copyright.
